title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. Every market price is an implicit forecast of future cash flows.
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett / Michael Mauboussin

web_blocks.html: On November 23, 2026, Coforge closed at ₹2,142.30 on the NSE (+2.66% 1D, +6.58% 1W) [24]. Market cap stood at ₹95,036.98 Cr across 44.31 Cr shares after a routine ESOP allotment [24, 30]. A later TradingView snapshot (Nov 25) showed a -3.84% pullback to ₹2,060.00, putting the stock at 40.43x TTM P/E and 4.08x P/B [24]. TTM sales grew 41.21% YoY and EPS rose 47.37% YoY [24]. Backward earnings understate merged scale. Q2 FY27 sales hit ₹6,170.8 Cr (~₹24,683 Cr annualized), backed by a $2.38 billion 12-month order book (+45% YoY) and 16.0% FY27 EBIT margin guidance [5].

Does this price offer real upside, or does it ignore post-Encora risks? We run two checks. First, a Reverse DCF solves for the 10-year free cash flow growth baked into ~₹95,037 Cr of equity value plus ~₹4,800 Cr of net debt [1, 24, 38]. Second, a Peer Snapshot Table compares Coforge against Persistent Systems, LTTS, KPIT, and Mphasis on live multiples [24, 25, 26, 27, 28].

web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹2,142.30 (EV ~₹99,837 Cr), the market embeds ~16.6% 10-year FCF CAGR at an 11.5% discount rate. We refuse to chase rallies and keep our ₹2,620 Base target capped at 32.8x FY28E EPS until Total DSO drops below 90 days.

web_blocks.takeaway: Coforge trades at 40.43x TTM P/E, a 24.5% discount to Persistent (53.58x), despite +41.21% TTM sales growth and matching 15.50% OPM. It holds a justified growth premium over Mphasis (24.18x), LTTS (28.81x), and Stage-4 KPIT (26.46x).

web_blocks.title: Why the 24.5% Persistent Discount Persists—and What Closes It
paragraphs: Persistent Systems trades at 53.58x TTM P/E because its growth is organic and net-cash [24, 25]. Coforge issued 93.8M shares (~21.8% stake) to Advent and Warburg at ₹1,815.91 and took on ₹6,026 Cr of debt (CRISIL AA+/Stable) to buy Encora [1, 6, 35, 38]. That pulled headline ROE down to 13.46% [24].

Pass 1 also flagged two overhangs that cap multiple expansion today. Q2 FY27 Total DSO stretched +8 days QoQ to 110 days (net unbilled ₹2,600 Cr), and Chairman O.P. Bhatt plus NRC Chair D.K. Singh resigned in September 2026 [33, 34, 36]. Meanwhile, FX hedge losses ($10.2M in Q2) drop to zero in FY28, and a ~55% US mix plus LatAm hubs buffer H-1B visa fees [36, 37, 39]. If Q3–Q4 FY27 delivers Encora growth, DSO below 90 days, and a permanent Chair, FY28E EPS can reach ₹80 and justify ₹2,620 (32.8x).

web_blocks.html: Five-year valuation bands look balanced, not euphoric. Coforge has traded between 24x (2022–23 pause) and 55x (2021 peak), with a 38x–40x median [1]. At 40.43x TTM P/E—about 26x–27x annualized H2 FY27E earnings—it sits near its median multiple ahead of November 30 MSCI EM Index inclusion [24, 32].

Valuation Trigger: We keep our Base target at ₹2,620.00 (32.8x FY28E EPS of ₹80). If Q3 or Q4 FY27 shows Encora revenue shrinking QoQ, Total DSO stuck above 110 days, or EBIT margin below 15.0%, FY28E EPS falls toward ₹62 and forces a 26x Bear de-rating (₹1,620).

book_paragraphs: Now you and I step out of the price-blind room and look at the live ticker tape. On the verified November 23, 2026 NSE session, Coforge closed at ₹2,142.30—up 6.58% over the prior week—before pulling back 3.84% to ₹2,060.00 on the November 25 TradingView snapshot. At roughly ₹95,037 Cr of market capitalization across 44.31 Cr shares, the stock trades at 40.43x trailing twelve-month earnings and 4.08x book value.

At first glance, forty times trailing earnings looks steep next to legacy Indian IT majors. Yet backward twelve-month numbers still blend pre-Encora quarters with only partial post-merger earnings. In Q2 FY27 alone, the combined Coforge-Encora platform generated ₹6,170.8 Cr in revenue—an annualized run rate near ₹24,700 Cr—backed by a record $2.38 billion 12-month executable order book (+45% YoY) and upgraded 16.0% full-year FY27 EBIT margin guidance.

To test whether ₹2,142.30 is cheap or demanding, let us run a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow model. Adding roughly ₹4,800 Cr of post-Encora net debt brings enterprise value near ₹99,837 Cr. At an 11.5% cost of capital and a 5.0% terminal growth rate, the market price implies roughly a 16.6% compound annual growth rate in free cash flow over the next decade. That hurdle is achievable, but it leaves no room for sloppy execution or chasing extended rallies.

Comparing Coforge side-by-side against its four closest Indian peers on the exact same November 2026 snapshot sharpens the picture. Persistent Systems—the organic, net-cash digital engineering benchmark—trades at 53.58x TTM P/E at ₹6,120. L&T Technology Services trades at 28.81x at ₹4,178, KPIT Technologies sits in Stage 4 at 26.46x (₹516), and Mphasis trades at 24.18x (₹2,532.90). Coforge at 40.43x commands a 24.5% valuation discount to Persistent despite posting 41.21% YoY revenue growth and matching Persistent's 15.50% TTM operating margin.

Why does that 13-turn P/E discount to Persistent remain stubbornly wide? Our Pass 1 blind-spot audit answered that question honestly. First, Coforge took on ₹6,026 Cr of borrowings (CRISIL AA+/Stable) and issued 93.8 million shares (~21.8% stake) to Advent International and Warburg Pincus to close Encora, temporarily lowering ROE to 13.46%. Second, Q2 FY27 Total DSO stretched eight days sequentially to 110 days as net unbilled revenue climbed to ₹2,600 Cr during US-to-India entity novations. Third, the abrupt September 2026 resignations of Chairman O.P. Bhatt and NRC Chair D.K. Singh introduced a boardroom governance overhang through January 2027. Until those three overhangs clear, we refuse to stretch our valuation multiple beyond 32.8x FY28E earnings, holding our Base target firmly at ₹2,620.

Look also at what sits below the operating line, because non-operating friction often hides future earnings power. In Q2 FY27, Coforge absorbed $10.2 million in legacy foreign-exchange hedge losses, dragging Other Income into negative territory. Management has laid out an explicit runoff schedule: hedge losses taper to $7.1–$7.5 million in Q3 FY27, fall to $1.2 million in Q4 FY27, and vanish completely in FY28 as the $550 million fixed-rate USD term loan provides a natural balance-sheet hedge. Removing that non-operating headwind creates a clean earnings bridge even before assuming any multiple expansion.

Finally, consider five-year valuation history. Between 2021 and 2026, Coforge traded as low as 24x earnings during the 2022–23 tech spending pause and as high as 55x at the 2021 peak, with a median near 38x to 40x. At 40.43x trailing P/E—roughly 26x to 27x annualized H2 FY27 run-rate earnings—the stock is priced near its historical midpoint while carrying its largest executable backlog on record.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why We Refused to Raise the Target Price
book_callouts.text: When a stock rallies from ₹2,010 to ₹2,142, the temptation is to bump the target price to justify chasing. We did the opposite. Because our Pass 1 audit uncovered a 110-day Total DSO spike and a boardroom governance transition, we kept our Base target anchored at ₹2,620 (32.8x FY28E EPS of ₹80)—forcing price to come back into our ₹1,952–₹2,036 support zone before adding capital.

book_subsections.title: Deconstructing the 16.6% Implied FCF Hurdle & FX Runoff Tailwind
paragraphs: At ₹99,837 Cr of enterprise value, clearing a 16.6% ten-year FCF CAGR requires two engines working in tandem. The first is top-line durability: the $2.38 billion executable order book covers roughly 85% of next-twelve-month revenue, while the November 25 Nuuron agentic cybersecurity launch deepens enterprise AI penetration. The second is cash conversion and non-operating cleanup: H1 FY27 FCF/PAT already improved to 92% ($53.8M in Q2), and legacy FX hedge losses ($10.2M in Q2) are scheduled to taper to $7.1–$7.5M in Q3, $1.2M in Q4, and zero in FY28 as the $550M USD term loan acts as a natural hedge.

If Coforge converts 85% to 95% of net profit into free cash flow and retires ₹1,500–₹2,000 Cr of debt per year, CRISIL's projection of net debt/EBITDA falling below 1.0x over the medium term becomes reality—transferring enterprise value steadily from lenders back to shareholders.

book_subsections.title: Peer Multiples, US Visa Exposure & Passive MSCI Flows
paragraphs: Within Indian mid-tier IT, quality and macro exposure diverge sharply. KPIT (26.46x) and LTTS (28.81x) remain exposed to European and Detroit auto R&D pauses, while Mphasis (24.18x) faces slower top-line momentum. Furthermore, higher US H-1B visa fees ($100,000 for new petitions) weigh more heavily on peers deriving 75%–80% of revenue from the United States. Coforge's ~55% US revenue mix and Encora's Latin American nearshore engineering hubs provide a tangible structural buffer.

Near-term technical demand also receives a mechanical boost from Coforge's inclusion in the MSCI Global Standard / Emerging Markets Index effective November 30, 2026. Yet index inflows are a temporary liquidity event, not a permanent moat. Long-term multiple expansion from 40x toward 45x depends strictly on Encora resuming organic growth in Q3 FY27 and Total DSO stepping back below 90 days.

book_subsections.title: Sensitivity Check: Governance & Working-Capital Downside
paragraphs: Stress-testing our model is essential when a company carries ₹6,026 Cr of debt and an interim Chair. Suppose Encora's contract novations drag into Q4 FY27, keeping Total DSO above 105 days and capping consolidated EBIT margin at 15.0%, while Advent or Warburg trims part of its 21.8% rollover stake once lock-ups expire. Under that stress scenario, FY28E EPS would compress toward ₹62 and the market would likely de-rate Coforge to 26x forward earnings—our ₹1,620 Bear target.

Conversely, if Q3–Q4 FY27 delivers 16.5%–17.0% EBIT margins, Encora matches core Coforge growth, and a respected permanent independent Chair takes office cleanly, FY28E EPS can reach ₹84. At 35.1x forward earnings—still a steep discount to Persistent's 53.58x trailing multiple—the stock supports our ₹2,950 Bull target.
